ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP identification under Ley 10/2010, art. 13; screening of all UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against SEPBLAC databases, the United Nations Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Reg. (EU) 269/2014 and related instruments), and the OFAC SDN List where any USD payment rails are contemplated; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth documentation required for any PEP or PEP-linked beneficial owner; breaches subject to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 under Ley 10/2010, art. 57.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online negative-name certificate via www.rmc.es or the Colegio de Registradores de España telematics portal (Proyecto RMC)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Articles 401–413 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RRM): the proposed corporate denomination must be written in Spanish or fully transliterated into Latin script with Spanish spelling, must include the legal-form suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.', and must not be identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to a pre-existing or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RMC rejects the proposed name or the certificate expires, a new application (solicitud) must be filed at the RMC; the rejection decision may be appealed by filing a recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP, Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Cortes) within one month of notification; the DGSJFP must decide within three months; an adverse decision or silence can be challenged before the Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the applicant's address.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: a Spanish S.L. may register a professional co-working or managed-office address in Spain (a P.O. Box alone is inadmissible), provided the address is a genuine physical situs and a verified occupancy contract is produced for notarial and registry purposes. For the ISIC 4100 hospital-medical-gas licensee holding a health-authority installation authorization, additional operational substance (technical manager, project documentation, tooling access) is expected; a virtual-only office will be accepted by the Registry but will trigger enhanced AML due diligence and may be refused by public-sector healthcare contracting authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 20–30% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first operating year, comprising Consejería de Sanidad technical inspections of licensed medical gas installers, Inspección de Trabajo site visits, and notarial or Registro Mercantil verification visits triggered by any inconsistency in registered-office or UBO data; the risk increases substantially if the registered office is a bare virtual address without a dedicated compliance officer.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) – arts. 20-23 (public deed constitution), art. 28 (registered office), arts. 36-69 (minimum capital and contributions), arts. 124-125 (corporate purpose). Also Royal Decree 1483/2012 (General Accounting Plan).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for name reservation; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) at the registered office for registration and inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (notarised deed of incorporation) registered in the Mercantile Registry; accompanied by Form 036 for the provisional Tax Identification Code (NIF).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an SL, the statutory minimum is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid at execution of the public deed. The amount must be deposited in a bank account opened in the future company's name and evidenced by a bank certificate to the notary; no separate escrow account or escrow agent is required. The deposit becomes freely available after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The share capital of this Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada shall be the statutory minimum, EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid by the founding members. The capital subscription, contribution and representation are accepted. 2. The registered office is adopted as set forth in the articles of association, located in Spain. The sole administrator is authorised to sign leases and register the address. 3. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Administrador Único, and [Name] as joint legal representative for tax and social security matters. The administrator is authorised to execute, present and file the incorporation deed, obtain the provisional and definitive Tax ID, register the company with the Commercial Registry, publish in BORME, and take all ancillary steps. This resolution has effect from signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) via the Punto de Acceso General online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application on the Registro Mercantil Central system proposing up to three distinctive company names. The system checks identical or confusingly similar names against registered Spanish and EU companies. Once approved, the negative name certificate is issued electronically and is valid for three months. The certificate must be produced to the notary when executing the deed.
required_dossiers: DNI or NIE of all founding partners
Proposed company names in order of preference
Description of corporate purpose (ISIC 4100, medical gas pipeline installation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any proposed name is refused or queried, resubmit a new proposal through the same portal; a refusal may be challenged before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month. The certificate must be kept valid through registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit statutory minimum capital and obtain bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notaría) and Spanish credit institution (banco)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account in the name of 'the company being formed' (or in the name of all subscribers as joint account holders). Deposit at least €3,000 by each subscriber pro rata to their participation. Obtain a bank certificate (certificado de depósito) listing each contributor, the total amount, and the account number. The certificate is annexed to the public deed and is revoked after registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all subscribers
Bank deposit certificate
Valuation report if any in-kind contribution is made
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate contains discrepancies regarding subscriber names or capital amounts, request the bank to reissue the certificate with the exact identity data to be used in the deed. In-kind contributions must be described in the deed with a valuation report by an expert if required by the Capital Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute public deed of incorporation and apply for provisional NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (Civil Law Notary) and Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – opening tax registry office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear before a Spanish notary to execute the Escritura de Constitución. The deed includes the articles of association (Estatutos), the registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, administrator's appointment, and the method of board deliberation. After execution, the notary or the founders file Form 036 with AEAT to obtain a provisional Tax Identification Code (NIF). The provisional NIF is mandatory before commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate
Draft articles of association (Estatutos)
Founders' valid DNI/NIE/passports
Notarised power of attorney if a representative appears
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects defects in the articles or capital payment, the deed draft is corrected and the execution is rescheduled. If AEAT rejects or queries the provisional NIF application, submit corrected Form 036 with missing or rectified information and, if necessary, provide the notary's certification of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after execution of the deed, deposit the 'primera copia' (first authorised copy) of the deed at the Provincial Commercial Registry. The registrar reviews the deed against legal requirements and issues an inscription. After the qualification, the company acquires legal personality. The registry automatically shares the inscription with the Official Gazette (BORME) for publication. Once the registration certificate is issued, the provisional NIF can converted to the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
Provisional NIF certificate
Proof of payment of Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (AJD) on incorporation
Certificate of registered office, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'nota de calificación' suspending or refusing registration, the founders may remedy the defect by amending the deed or supplying the missing documentation and resubmitting. If disagreement persists, the founders may lodge an appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security and municipal formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS), and local municipal licensing offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription in the Commercial Registry, finalise the definitive NIF through AEAT user account or Form 036. Register the company with the economic activities census (censo de obligados tributarios) and obtain a VAT registration. Open a formal corporate bank current account. Register the employer code with TGSS before hiring staff. Obtain the corresponding municipal construction and operating licences for the project site before starting any installation works.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry inscription certificate
Definitive NIF notice
Completed Form 036/037 tax census declaration
Company current account statement as proof of capital availability
Municipal licence application forms for the intended worksite
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT does not convert the provisional NIF within the expected period, submit a written request using Form 036 attaching the registry certificate. For TGSS, employer registration is mandatory within ten days of the first hire; any delay is cured by immediate retroactive registration plus possible penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria of the relevant Autonomous Community (Industrial Registry for companies installing medical gases) and the municipal department responsible for the construction/installation licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Instalación y Puesta en Servicio de Instalaciones de Gases Medicinales (Medical Gas Pipeline System Installation and Commissioning Authorisation) and registration as 'Empresa Instaladora Autorizada de Gases Medicinales'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community / Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría: Actividad sujeta a licencia municipal de actividades clasificadas; full Environmental Impact Assessment is generally not required for interior medical gas pipe installation. Exemption applies where the project affects only building internal spaces, with no significant discharge, emission or land contamination.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with UNE-EN ISO 7396-1 for medical gas pipeline systems; pressure tests must be performed with validated protocols. No routine wastewater discharge arises from the piping installation; any incidental brazing or soldering emissions must not cause occupational exposure limits under RD 374/2001 to be exceeded. Waste copper, fittings and soldering residues are managed in accordance with Law 22/2011 on Waste and Contaminated Soils; any atmospheres containing oxygen require housekeeping and clean-gas-handling provisions consistent with ISO 7396-1 and pressurised equipment directive RD 2060/2008.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate per RD 513/2017 issued by an authorised inspection body; structural load verification for manifold supports and ceiling penetrations under the Spanish Technical Building Code (CTE) and RD 314/2006; workplace health and safety clearance under Law 31/1995 and RD 486/1997, including verification that oxygen/medical gas storage areas are properly ventilated, separated from hazardous materials and accessible for emergency services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT Electronic Office (Sede Electrónica). The common Spanish VAT and corporate tax regime applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands; the Basque Country and Navarra have separate historical tax administrations, and the Canary Islands apply IGIC rather than mainland Spanish VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a provisional NIF and then a definitive NIF through the AEAT, normally using Form 036, with incorporation deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered address, and identification of directors and authorized representatives. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities or required to interact with Spanish tax authorities must obtain a Spanish NIF, generally by filing Form 036 with the competent AEAT office or through an authorized representative. Foreign corporate documents must normally be legalized or apostilled, accompanied by an official Spanish translation where required, and include evidence of the entity's legal existence, registered address, ownership or control information where requested, and the powers and tax identification of its representative. A Spanish VAT number is the Spanish NIF prefixed by ES and is activated through registration in the Census of Business Persons, Professionals and Withholding Agents. Registration should be completed before commencing taxable activities, making intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, importing goods, or issuing invoices requiring Spanish VAT identification. The intra-Community VAT operator register (ROI/VIES) must be requested where intra-Community transactions require it. A non-established business may additionally need a Spanish fiscal representative for particular non-EU VAT refund or compliance procedures, although Spain generally does not impose a universal VAT fiscal-representative requirement on every non-established taxable person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Spanish SL is a separate taxpayer for Spanish Corporate Income Tax and is generally taxed on its worldwide accounting profit, subject to statutory adjustments, exemptions, participation exemptions, loss utilization limits, transfer-pricing rules, and applicable tax treaties. Spanish tax residence generally follows incorporation under Spanish law, registered office, or effective management in Spain. The SL is not automatically fiscally transparent merely because it has limited liability. A Spanish SL may qualify for specific reduced rates or incentives, including regimes applicable to newly created entities, but those regimes do not convert it into a pass-through entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. Separate legal entities are ordinarily subject to Corporate Income Tax. Available elections or optional regimes may include the Spanish consolidated Corporate Income Tax regime for qualifying groups, the special VAT group regime, the special VAT cash-accounting regime where statutory conditions are met, the monthly VAT refund regime and REDEME registration, and voluntary or mandatory SII reporting depending on taxpayer status. Certain transparent-entity, permanent-establishment, investment, restructuring, holding-company, and tax-haven rules may apply by operation of law or under specific statutory conditions. Spanish anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD 2 can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict relief for payments involving hybrid entities, hybrid instruments, imported mismatches, or dual-resident arrangements; there is no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Spanish Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA). Mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands use VAT; the Canary Islands use the Impuesto General Indirecto Canario (IGIC), while Ceuta and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of EU VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0. Spain has no general turnover threshold below which a person making taxable economic activities is automatically outside VAT registration. A taxable person must register in the census before commencing a taxable activity or conducting transactions requiring VAT identification. Separate thresholds and conditions may apply to specific special schemes, distance sales, intra-Community acquisitions, imports, and EU-wide small-business rules. A hospital engineering EPC contractor must assess VAT registration, domestic reverse charge, intra-Community transactions, import VAT, and the place-of-supply rules for installation and construction-related services. The Spanish domestic reverse charge may apply to qualifying construction, installation, and subcontracting services connected with construction or rehabilitation works when statutory conditions are satisfied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every private-sector invoice. The electronic invoicing framework under Law 18/2022 and its implementing regulations will introduce mandatory B2B electronic invoicing in phases after the applicable technical and regulatory commencement dates. Public-sector supplies generally require structured electronic invoices through the designated public-sector platforms, including FACe where applicable. The SII system requires qualifying taxpayers, including large businesses, VAT groups, REDEME entities, and voluntary participants, to transmit VAT invoice-record data electronically to the AEAT, generally within four business days subject to statutory exclusions and adjustments. Tax software is subject to integrity, traceability, accessibility, and anti-tampering requirements under the invoicing-system rules, including Royal Decree 1007/2023 and subsequent implementation measures; applicable deadlines and technical requirements must be verified at deployment. Electronic signatures, QR or verification data, digital records, and retention controls may be required depending on the invoicing system and recipient. Electronic invoicing does not itself replace customs evidence, VAT books, or transaction-level proof of export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the supplier retains reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The exemption is not available merely because the customer is non-resident or pays from a foreign bank account. Evidence normally includes the export customs declaration, MRN and electronic exit confirmation, transport documentation, commercial invoice, order and delivery records, and accounting records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for the applicable VAT exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies recapitulative-statement and evidentiary requirements. Services supplied to a business established outside the EU are generally outside the scope of Spanish VAT under the business-to-business place-of-supply rule, rather than technically zero-rated; exceptions apply to services connected with immovable property, admission to events, passenger transport, short-term transport hiring, and other special categories. Export-related logistics, installation, and engineering services require transaction-specific place-of-supply analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory, or equivalent customs-certified exit evidence
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, Incoterms where used, and VAT treatment
Bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or other transport document demonstrating dispatch to the non-EU destination
Purchase order, contract, packing list, delivery records, and warehouse or carrier evidence linking the goods to the export declaration
Accounting records, VAT books, export-sales ledger, and evidence of reporting in the relevant VAT return
Customer identification and, for intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and recapitulative-statement evidence
Bank payment or settlement evidence where relevant; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT export document and does not substitute for customs exit evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for claiming export VAT exemption or input-VAT recovery. Export proceeds may remain abroad subject to ordinary accounting, anti-money-laundering, customs, transfer-pricing, and financial-reporting obligations. AEAT audits focus on actual exit from the EU, consistency between customs and VAT records, transport evidence, customer status, correct place-of-supply treatment, and absence of sham or diverted transactions. If zero-rating or exemption is unsupported, the supplier may be required to pay the undercharged VAT retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and applicable surcharges, while input-VAT deductions or refunds may be denied or clawed back. Inaccurate or fraudulent VAT treatment can attract proportional tax penalties commonly ranging from 50% to 150% of the improperly omitted or unduly refunded tax, depending on the infringement and aggravating circumstances, in addition to record-keeping and invoicing penalties. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold of EUR 120,000 of tax per fiscal year may constitute a criminal offense under Spanish law, with potential fines and imprisonment. Customs penalties, seizure, loss of preferential treatment, and coordinated VAT recovery may also apply where export documentation is falsified or goods did not leave the EU.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), the national central bank within the Eurosystem, exercises monetary operations, balance-of-payments statistics and the foreign-transaction declaration regime under Royal Decree 1835/2010. Foreign-investment screening and registry functions are attributed to the Directorate General for International Trade and Investments (DGCTI) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business; the exchange-control legal framework is completed by Article 63 TFEU, Royal Decree 1816/1991, and Order ETD/22/2023.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full current-account and capital-account liberalisation under Article 63 TFEU and Title IV of Royal Decree 1816/1991; the euro is fully convertible and no prior exchange-control authorisation applies to equity injections, profit remittances, supplier payments or shareholder loans. Dividends and branch profits are remittable after the 25% corporate income tax levy, subject to Non-Resident Income Tax withholding at the statutory 19% for EU/EEA and treaty-eligible recipients, or a reduced DTT rate under Spain's Latin American treaties (typically 5%-15% for substantial shareholdings); 21% applies only to non-cooperative tax-haven jurisdictions. A post-investment foreign-investment declaration to the DGCTI is required when the inbound investment exceeds EUR 1,250,000 or reaches 10% of the SL capital; this filing is statistical and not an authorisation bar. No capital controls, quarantine periods, or prior clearance delays apply to euro-denominated or foreign-currency movements through resident banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender obligation, a 0% mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds; exporters may retain 100% of receipts in EUR or foreign-currency settlement accounts held domestically or abroad. The only binding rule is statistical: foreign-trade settlements exceeding EUR 1,250,000 per settlement event must be declared to Banco de España under Order ETD/22/2023 (replacing the former EUR 50,000 per-operation threshold), and all settlements remain subject to standard invoicing, customs-export documentation and transfer-pricing substance rules. A 90-day conversion into EUR is recommended treasury policy, not law, to neutralise EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm-currency volatility on the EPC working-capital cycle.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta de garantía) plus Operational Account (cuenta operativa)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BBVA — Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, S.A.
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with FX forward line and trade/LC desk
Capital Escrow Account for hospital contract retentions and Operational Account
Operational Account for SEPA supplier disbursements
Operational Account (secondary rail and FX derivative line)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for EUR pass-through disbursement rails; LOW for statutory banking instruments. A foreign-authorised digital EMI (e.g., UK, Lithuania, Germany) cannot settle Healthcare_Authority_Wire payments because Spanish public-health treasuries disburse through Iberpay/TARGET2, an infrastructure to which non-member EMIs lack direct access. EMIs are also legally incapable of issuing 'avales' or 'garantías definitivas' required under Spanish public procurement (Law 9/2017 on Public Sector Contracts) and cannot hold irrevocable escrow/retention mandates for hospital EPC works. A Banco de España-registered or EU-passported EMI may open an ES IBAN for operational overheads, but the SL must maintain its primary treasury relationship, contract guarantees and hedging lines with a fully licensed Spanish credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate under Law 10/2010 and EU AMLD4/5: a Spanish-resident managing director may open accounts fully remotely using an eIDAS-qualified digital certificate (DNI electrónico) and video identification; non-resident directors and beneficial owners must produce a notarised power of attorney, apostilled or consular-legalised for non-Hague jurisdictions, granted before a Spanish notary, the Spanish Consulate, or a local notary, with in-branch execution of the banking mandate. Physical presence is de facto mandatory for the signatory opening escrow/guarantee accounts and for activating multi-signature (2-of-3) payment rules on hospital retention accounts; the expected onboarding window for a non-resident-owned ES_SL is 2-4 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) resident outside the EU, or a corporate chain containing a nominee/offshore layer, triggering a higher-risk classification under Article 4 of Law 10/2010 and EBA risk-factor guidelines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled parent certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; full corporate-organisation chart to final natural persons; tax residence certificates of all UBOs; notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; three years of audited ultimate-parent financial statements or a certified book-debt declaration; written narrative on the EPC hospital-medical-gas pipeline business, public-health payer base, and ISIC/NAICS scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Equity capital wired before the capital increase is inscribed in the Registro Mercantil, a pattern flagged as potential front-loading of unverified funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Public deed of capital increase (escritura de ampliación de capital); the notary's certificate of cash deposit (certificación del desembolso) required by Article 62 of the Capital Companies Law; a dated board commitment to file for inscription within the statutory 2-month window; a copy of the Banco de España foreign-transaction declaration and, where applicable, the DGCTI foreign-investment filing reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity pay-outs to non-EU equipment suppliers (copper tube, vacuum pumps, terminal manifolds) without an evidentiary chain, creating a trade-mismatch red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle of purchase orders, supplier commercial invoices, CMR/Bill of Lading, DUA/SAD customs declarations and inspection certificates; ISO 7396-1 and UNE 7396-1 medical-gas-system compliance certificates; bank-purpose narrative 'pago de importación de bienes de equipo sanitario'; matching letter-of-credit or documentary-collection records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts routed through intermediaries from Latin American hospital or health-ministry payers, triggering PEP and sanctions-led enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the public-procurement award or framework contract with the health authority; PEP questionnaire and identity evidence of the payer's authorised signatory; certification of works (certificación de obra) and payment certificates; where relevant, the EIB/IDB/CAF or development-bank funding agreement evidencing the disbursement chain; a sanctions legal opinion (EU, UK, OFAC) covering the counterparty jurisdiction and project corridor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (1) segregate shareholder funds in the originator's account; (2) send an SWIFT MT103 wire to the SL's Spanish IBAN with the memo 'Aportación de capital — escritura de ampliación de capital de [date]', settling in EUR via SEPA/EBA or TARGET2; (3) file the applicable Banco de España foreign-transaction declaration (declaración de operaciones con el exterior) for the inflow and, when the investment exceeds EUR 1,250,000 or 10% ownership, file the DGCTI post-investment declaration through the electronic registry within the statutory window; (4) retain the notarial certificate of deposit as the bank's compliance evidence pack. For shareholder loans, execute a documented 'préstamo participativo' or ordinary shareholder-loan agreement, disclose the lender's Spanish NIF, and clear interest and principal remittances against the same declaration framework; treaty-favourable withholding requires the lender's tax residence certificate and a beneficial-ownership statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer through Iberpay for Spanish and EU suppliers — the same rail used by hospital treasuries for Healthcare_Authority_Wire settlement of the SL's progress certificates; (b) SWIFT MT103 for extra-SEPA suppliers and payments above EUR 50,000; (c) Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 (issued via SWIFT MT700) for high-value imports of manifolds, vacuum pumps and copper systems, with confirmation requested where the supplier's bank requires it; (d) Documentary Collections (CAD) for routine Latin American vendor shipments. Contract retentions must be parked in an escrow/guarantee account pledged to the hospital authority by an irrevocable 'mandato de disposición de garantía'; treasury must reconcile certification-triggered settlements monthly to avoid VAT and corporate-income-tax timing mismatches.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards ('seguros de cambio') with Spanish or EU-licensed banks, tenors up to 12 months, documented against underlying EPC contracts and invoices, executed under ISDA or FBF master agreements and subject to EMIR trade reporting.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on non-fully-convertible Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, PEN) where physical offshore settlement is impossible, supported by underlying tender and contract exposure dossiers.
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) converting project-finance liabilities from EUR into USD or LatAm-currency baskets, subject to EMIR reporting and clearing-threshold assessment.
European-style currency options to cap tender and bid-stage exposure on hospital-authority projects, with premiums capitalised into bid pricing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approve within six months after financial year-end; file within one month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, filing is normally due by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry filing fee is tariff-based and not a single national fixed amount. Late filing may cause registry closure, prevent registration of further corporate documents, and expose directors to liability; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, 1 to 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax due generally triggers fixed percentage penalties subject to statutory reductions; tax due may attract late-payment interest and penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, depending on the infringement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party and tax-haven transactions information return (Modelo 232), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, normally 1 to 30 November of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or incorrect filing may trigger formal tax penalties, including fixed or transaction-based fines, and may increase transfer-pricing audit exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, normally by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization may result in registry closure affecting subsequent filings and may support director liability for defective bookkeeping.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual real beneficial owner declaration included with annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update and submit with the annual accounts filing; beneficial ownership changes should be recorded and reported through the applicable registry mechanism without undue delay.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may result in registry rejection, compliance escalation, and administrative sanctions under Spanish anti-money-laundering rules.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, and average employees of 50. Audit is also mandatory for certain regulated, public-interest, consolidated, or specially regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad). IFRS applies mandatorily to qualifying consolidated groups and may apply in permitted circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Confirm the ultimate beneficial owner when annual accounts are filed, update the declaration after any ownership or control change, and maintain supporting ownership and control records. A change in shareholding or control must also be reflected in the company's Register of Members and reported through the applicable beneficial ownership filing process.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,200 per year, approximately USD 325-1,300, excluding substantial mail handling, accounting, tax, or sector-licensing services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,500-8,000 per year, approximately USD 1,625-8,650, for a small Spanish SL; complex, regulated, or group entities may incur materially higher fees.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created entities engaged in economic activity during the first two taxable years, provided the entity has share capital of no more than €3,000 and qualifies as a small or medium-sized enterprise and is not part of a group. Tax credits available for R&D and technological innovation activities, job creation credits, and reinvestment of extraordinary income in Spanish territory. No general patent box benefit applicable to medical gas pipeline installation; standard deduction for impairment of receivables and amortization of goodwill permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) submitted via the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic portal, Sede Electrónica, using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve PIN or authorized representative with electronic signature
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end; for a December year-end entity, filing window runs from 1 July to 25 July. Quarterly interim prepayments (Modelo 202 or 222) filed during the taxable year based on prior-year taxable income, with payment in April, July, October, and December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover reported in the financial year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident Spanish SL must report gross turnover generated through its Spanish permanent establishment or Spanish-source activities, in euros, with no netting of expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base (base imponible), prior to offset of tax losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity computes Spanish PE attributable profits under the separate enterprise principle; all intercompany transactions must reflect arm's length consideration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforwards generated in prior years offset in the current period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SL may offset tax losses attributable to the Spanish PE, limited to 50% of the tax base for entities with net revenue over €20 million; entities under that threshold may offset up to 60% in 2025 and must wait until after the 5-year carryforward period. Offsetting cannot reduce the tax base below 50% of the pre-offset amount for entities meeting the revenue threshold, or below 25% for other entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and double taxation relief applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company can claim credit for withholding taxes suffered in Spain on income attributable to the PE and may apply DTA relief on dividends, interest, and royalties subject to a valid certificate of tax residence in the treaty state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total amount payable or resulting refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a non-resident SL has no PE, income subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) must be reported on Modelo 210; where a PE exists, the annual Modelo 200 is final settlement and quarterly Modelo 202 prepayments apply to the PE's taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice: penalty of 10% of the untendered amount if filed within 3 months after the deadline, plus 1% for each additional month of delay. After an AEAT formal request: 50% penalty of the payment due, with reduced surcharges if filed within 3 months of notification, escalating to 100% surcharge after 12 months. Late filing also accrues late payment interest (interés de demora) of 4.0625% for 2025, and a minimum fixed penalty may apply. For entities with a tax amount exceeding €15,000, failure to file by electronic means carries a separate formal infringement penalty of €400 to €2,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA) with Spain, the beneficial owner must obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction. The certificate must be presented, usually accompanied by a DTA relief claim; for dividends, the paying entity or depositary may apply the reduced treaty rate upon receipt before payment. For Spanish-source dividends distributed to an EU parent, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive mechanism allows a 0% withholding tax where the parent holds at least 5% of the SL share capital for at least 12 months and is tax resident in another EU member state or in an EEA state with an exchange of information agreement; excess withheld amounts may be claimed via refund procedures. Spain also transposes the EU Interest and Royalty Directive, reducing withholding to 0% for associated EU companies subject to a 25% direct or indirect shareholding, a two-year holding period, and substance requirements. Refund claims must generally be filed within four years from the end of the withholding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR rates: 19% on interest and 24% on royalties paid by a Spanish SL to non-residents. DTA rates commonly reduced: interest 0-10%, royalties 5-10% under the applicable OECD-modelled DTA. The EU Interest and Royalty Directive provides a 0% withholding tax on payments between associated companies of different EU member states subject to a 25% shareholding, two-year minimum holding period, and beneficial ownership, and may require a prior administrative procedure in the form of a residence certificate and, in Spain, a notification to the tax authorities for matching.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to the extent that Spanish transfer pricing law under Article 18 of Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades mandates that related-party transactions be valued at arm's length. Spain does not operate Caribbean-style ESR but the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula antielusión), substance-over-form doctrine under Article 13 of the General Tax Law, and the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) require the Spanish SL to maintain real business activity, physical presence proportionate to the hospital engineering EPC activity, qualified personnel, contractual substance, and economic ownership of assets and risks. A Spanish SL without adequate substance that merely channels medical gas pipeline installation back-to-back contracts is vulnerable to recharacterization under anti-abuse rules and denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Infracción Tributaria Grave / Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying financial statements, concealing hospital EPC revenues obtained from Spanish public health authorities, issuing false invoices for medical gas pipeline subcontractor costs, or using undisclosed bank accounts to receive payments, resulting in a tax shortfall exceeding €120,000 per taxable year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax offence (art. 305 Código Penal) punishable by imprisonment from 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount. Additionally, loss of entitlement to public subsidies, tax benefits, and government contracts for a period of up to 6 years. For non-criminal serious infringement, a proportional penalty between 50% and 100% of the tax amount plus late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable under the doctrine of levantamiento del velo (piercing of the corporate veil) for civil restitution to the tax authority, jointly and severally with the SL. Criminal liability extends personally to de facto and de jure administrators who knowingly ordered or facilitated the evasion; the court may impose travel bans within Spain and the Schengen area, seizure of personal assets, restriction on freedom of movement, and imprisonment. Tax liability can be shifted to personal assets under art. 42 Ley General Tributaria where the director caused or collaborated in the infringement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Entidad Carente de Sustancia)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Spanish SL files tax returns and invoices as a hospital medical gas pipeline EPC contractor but has no workers, no rental premises, no project management function, no technical equipment, and delegates the entire contractual performance to a related company in a low-tax jurisdiction; the entity serves exclusively to strip profits through service fees or to obtain EU Directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of imputed income; denial of tax residence benefits; denial of treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary / Interest-Royalty Directive relief; application of anti-abuse clause (art. 15 LIS) to disregard the legal form; potential imposition of tax on deemed income, plus late payment interest and penalties of 50% to 100% of the associated tax deficiency. Spanish General Tax Law art. 206 bis contains a specific sanction for abusive arrangements of up to 25% on the transaction amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed certificates of substance falsifying economic presence are personally liable for the tax debt and may be charged with falsification of company records under art. 390 Código Penal, subject to imprisonment from 3 to 6 years and disqualification from holding directorship positions in Spain. Travel restrictions and extradition proceedings may be ordered by the competent criminal court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Spanish SL purchases copper vacuum manifolds, medical oxygen terminal valves, and engineering services from a related non-resident supplier at inflated prices, eroding Spanish taxable profit, or fails to prepare and keep the mandatory Local File and Master File despite the entity's turnover exceeding the €1,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Correction of the tax base to arm's length value, application of an additional penalty of 15% of the corrected amount where documentation is absent or inaccurate, plus late payment interest. In cases where the corrected transaction is considered a sham, the adjustment may attract a 50% penalty. Transfer pricing documentation may trigger a formal requirement to submit Modelo 232 (annual related-party transaction return) with a filing deadline of 10 months after the fiscal year-end; each omission or inaccurate transaction carries a minimum penalty of €1,000, escalating up to €100,000 for hidden related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false transfer pricing studies or deliberately arranged overpricing may be jointly liable for the penalty under art. 42 LGT. In a criminal tax qualification, a director may be prosecuted for fraud or cooperative tax evasion; penalties include imprisonment and disqualification from managing companies in Spain for up to 10 years, non-cumulative with loss of public benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Modelo 232 Reporting and Public Contract Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SL receives payments from the healthcare authority via wire transfers or letters of credit but fails to file the annual related-party transaction return (Modelo 232), fails to maintain AML due diligence for its subcontractors, or participates in bid-rigging with competitors on Spanish public hospital tenders under ISIC 4100 activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-filing of Modelo 232: penalty from 1% to 5% of the total amount of related-party transactions, with minimums of €1,000 per data omission or inaccurate data, subject to a maximum of €100,000. AML omissions: administrative sanctions from €60,001 to €5,000,000 depending on entity size and seriousness, plus public debarment from contracting with public health authorities for up to 10 years. Bid-rigging (art. 262 Código Penal) imposes imprisonment from 6 months to 2 years, fines of up to 18 months' value, and special disqualification from public contracting for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for sanctions if they failed to prevent the AML deficiency; the financial penalty can be personally extended to directors who benefited from or tolerated the operation. For bid-rigging, the criminal sentence imposes automatic personal travel bans, prohibition on approaching the hospital contracting authority, and seizure of business assets; directors of the SL can be jointly ordered to compensate the public health authority up to the total project value. Travel bans and imprisonment remain applicable under the Spanish criminal procedural regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File / Late Filing of Modelo 200 and IRNR Formalities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Spanish SL (including a non-resident owned SL) fails to submit Modelo 200 electronically by 25 July after fiscal year-end, fails to file the quarterly prepayment Modelo 202, or distributes dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding and remitting the 19% tax to AEAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing surcharge: 10% within 3 months, plus 1% per additional month if no formal AEAT notice; 50% penalty if filed after AEAT request; 100% if filed after final assessment. Failure to withhold on dividend distributions to non-residents triggers a sanction equal to the unwithheld amount (up to 100% of the tax due), interest for late payment, and an infraction penalty of 50% of the amount. Personal liability may be shifted to the declarant administrator who signs the return with false data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instructed or participated in the omission of withholding on dividends or who signed fraudulent periodic returns are jointly and severally liable for the sanctions. In an aggravated criminal case, the director may face imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, a travel ban in Spanish territory, and mandatory judicial appearance; the court will additionally order the restoration of withheld sums to the Tax Agency, payable personally by the director if the company is insolvent.
